text:
tara: quick heads-up  I clicked an internal cross-link from /guides/deploy -> /platform/routing#cost-rules and got a 404 in prod after the docusaurus migration. anyone else?

evan: yep, saw that in the nightly linkcheck. looks like the heading used an inline math-like parentheses `(cost rules)` which docusaurus slugified differently.

marta: easiest fix is explicit id on the target heading: `### Cost rules {#cost-rules}`. please also avoid relying on autogenerated slugs for headings with parentheses or emoji.

tara: opened PR with the id + updated the 3 inbound links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4899. included a tiny integration test that builds and checks the fragment.

docbot: buildkite/docs-validate #1120 failed: missing fragment `/platform/routing#cost-rules` (exit=1).

evan: minor note: some files still have CRLF or no-blank-line before a codefence and docusaurus ignores the preceding heading. i added a pre-commit hook to warn on `heading
```` adjacency.

marta: rebased, ran local `yarn build` and `./tools/linkcheck/check_fragments.sh build`  linkcheck passes locally. marking PR ready.

docbot: buildkite/docs-validate #1122 succeeded: no missing fragments. merged at 1788881286.

tara: great. i'll add a short blurb to "Writing docs" about explicit header ids for headings containing parentheses, inline code, or emoji, plus the pre-commit hook note.

evan: thanks  also filing follow-up to scan legacy mkdocs slugs across /integrations/ and /guides/ to catch stray inbound links.

marta: perfect. closing the thread.
